summary.text: A 55-year-old frail-looking multiparous postmenopausal lady presented with anorexia and easy fatigability for one month and abdominal distention, decreased urine output, constipation and a mass coming out of the vagina for the last 10 days. Examination showed tense ascites, bilateral pedal oedema, cervical descent, cystocele, rectocele and a hard fixed mass on per-rectal examination.

Workup showed decreased proteins, raised lactate dehydrogenase, CA-125 and carcinoembryonic antigen, gross ascites and a solid cystic mass on ultrasound and CT with deposits reported in the liver, pancreas and gastro-oesophageal junction. Ascitic cytology was suggestive of a mucin secreting neoplasm and aspiration cytology reported adenocarcinoma. A preoperative diagnosis of FIGO stage IV ovarian carcinoma was made.

After the first uneventful cycle of paclitaxel and carboplatin-based chemotherapy, a painless gush of fluid through the vagina occurred during the second cycle, with a 3 × 3 cm posterior vaginal wall defect. Exploratory laparotomy with hysterectomy, bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy, omentectomy and appendicectomy was performed and the vaginal wall rent repaired in two layers; the postoperative course was uneventful.

Histopathology showed mucinous adenocarcinoma of the bilateral adnexal masses with omental deposits and no malignancy in the other specimens. Adjuvant paclitaxel and carboplatin was started 3 weeks postoperatively for 4 cycles. Post chemotherapy she appeared clinically well and radiologically tumour free with CA 125 of 38 IU/ml over 8 months of follow-up, with no adverse events.
